name: Ọlọruntóbi Václavek-Salele
role: Former union leader (Ferrogate Transit Workers Union), now raising two grandchildren on a reduced pension
location: The Shelf, Block 14 — a three-room unit he shares with his grandchildren, near Western and Division
description:
Ọlọruntóbi is a man who was built for louder rooms than the one he currently occupies. He is tall and loose-limbed, with the kind of face that was clearly handsome and has aged into something more interesting — deep sienna complexion, heavy brow, a jaw that still juts when he is angry. He has cosmetic tiger-stripe bioluminescence on his arms and collarbone, a geneware mod he got in his forties to celebrate the Union's successful Ferrogate walkout of 2172, and which now glows a gentle amber when the building's lights go down. His natural hair has gone grey-silver and he wears it in short locs. A subvocal transceiver is implanted at his throat — old union infrastructure, technically still active.

For sixteen years Tobi was the loudest, most tenacious shop steward and eventually regional director the Ferrogate Transit Workers Union ever produced. He won three collective agreements, survived two corporate union-busting campaigns, and was personally blacklisted by two Ferrogate senior executives. Then his daughter Comfort died of an untreated pulmonary infection in 2194 — a death he attributes directly to Helix Biosystems' pharmaceutical pricing, which the union had been fighting for years — and left behind two children aged four and seven. Tobi took them without a moment's hesitation and quietly stopped being the man who changed things, because he was suddenly the man who made breakfast.

core_fears: failing the grandchildren the way he failed to save their mother
that his years of union work genuinely changed nothing permanent
core_desires: to see Helix Biosystems face real consequences for pharmaceutical pricing
to give Dami and Kofi-Ren a better tier than he could achieve
coping_mechanisms: busyness — he does not sit still
telling the grandchildren edited stories about their mother that emphasize her strength
blind_spots: his grief has calcified into a very specific political target — he struggles to address grief in any other form
does not see how much Kofi-Ren is watching and internalizing his anger
psychology.secret: He knows who the Ferrogate executive was who personally ordered the data purge that destroyed evidence of the pharmaceutical partnership he was building a case against. The executive is retired, living comfortably in Grosse Pointe Enclosure. Tobi has the executive's home address and has had it for three years. He has done nothing.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Union oratory mixed with Block 14 street vernacular; code-switches fluidly based on audience; drops into formal rhetoric when emotional
speech_patterns.cadence: Naturally rhetorical — builds to emphasis, uses repetition for effect; softens completely around the grandchildren
verbal_tics: Tapping the table with two fingers when making a point
example_lines: 'They don't win because they're stronger. They win because we keep being surprised that they'll actually do it. Stop being surprised. Then we can talk about winning.'
'Dami, eat. Kofi-Ren, I can see you. Eat your food and then you can show me your rig work, yes.'

story_hooks: Kofi-Ren has been approached by someone recruiting young people for direct action against Helix Biosystems — Tobi has found evidence of this and is terrified, not because he disagrees with the cause but because he knows exactly how it ends
A younger union organizer has uncovered the same pharmaceutical partnership evidence Tobi once had, and has come to him for guidance — reigniting everything he put away
narrative_function: Quest giver for labor and corporate accountability storylines; access point to Ferrogate Transit insider knowledge and union network; emotionally complex figure whose activism is dormant but not dead; the grandchildren can be a vulnerability or a source of motivation
augmentations: Tiger-stripe bioluminescent geneware (arms and collarbone, amber-gold) — cosmetic, personal significance; subvocal transceiver (throat implant, FTW Union network standard issue — technically still connected)
daily_life: Gets the grandchildren — Dami, 10, and Kofi-Ren, 13 — up and fed and to their learning pods by 0730, then spends the morning doing odd-job consulting for younger union members who call him for advice. Afternoons he does building maintenance for reduced rent. Evenings are homework, dinner, and whatever drama the Block 14 neighbors bring to his door.
affiliation: Ferrogate Transit Workers Union (retired regional director, still listed as emeritus); The Shelf Block 14 informal community network

decision_rules: The grandchildren come before everything, always
Never cross a picket line, in any context, metaphorically or literally
Don't spend anger before you know what you need it to accomplish
escalation_ladder: Asking precise questions that reveal he knows more than expected
Stating exactly what he knows and who he can reach with it
Calling in old union network favors — he still has them

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Friendly, slightly performative warmth — he is assessing whether they are labor or management energy before deciding how much to trust them
interpersonal_modes.friends: Deeply loyal, occasionally overbearing, will show up with food and unsolicited opinions in equal measure

stress_responses.low: Gets very loud and animated, paces, talks through problems to anyone nearby
stress_responses.medium: Goes quiet and organizing — starts writing things down, making contact lists
stress_responses.high: Focuses with frightening intensity on a single immediate task, delegates everything else without discussion

contradictions: Believes collective action is the only answer but has been handling his grief in radical isolation
Will deliver powerful speeches about courage but has not acted on the one thing he most wants to act on
habits: Makes elaborate breakfasts — the grandchildren's nutrition is his externalized anxiety management
Keeps a handwritten ledger of every favor given and received in the Block 14 network
Refers to his subvocal transceiver as 'the wire' and checks it is still active every morning
breaking_points: One of the grandchildren being harmed or threatened
Learning the Ferrogate executive has been profiting further from Helix Biosystems partnership
